sanskrit: etat te devaḥ savitā vāso dadātu bhartave | tat tvaṃ yamasya rājye vasānas tārpyaṃ cara ||
english: May the god Savitṛ give you this garment to wear; clad in it, may you walk satisfied in the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: dhānā dhenur bhavad vatso asyās tilo 'bhavat | tāṃ tvaṃ yamasya rājye +'kṣitām upa jīvatāt ||
english: The parched grains became a milch-cow; sesame became her calf. In the realm of Yama, may you live by means of her who is inexhaustible.

sanskrit: etās te asau dhānāḥ kāmadughā bhavantu | enīḥ śyenīr virūpāḥ sarūpās tilavatsā upa tiṣṭhantu tvāt ||
english: May these parched grains of yours become wish-fulfilling cows — tawny ones, swift as falcons, of varied forms and uniform forms, with sesame as their calves — let them attend upon you.

sanskrit: enīr dhānā hariṇīḥ śyenīr āsu kṛṣṇā dhānā hariṇīr dhenavas te | tilavatsā ūrjam asmai duhānā viśvahā santv anapasphurantīḥ ||
english: Tawny-grained, fawn-coloured, swift as falcons — among these the dark-grained, fawn-hued milch-cows are yours; with sesame as calves, ever yielding nourishment for him, may they be unfailing for all time.

sanskrit: vaiśvānare havir idaṃ juhomy etaṃ sāhasraṃ śatadhāram utsam | sa bibharat pitaraṃ pitāmahaṃ prapitāmahān bibharat pinvamānaḥ ||
english: I pour this oblation into Vaiśvānara — this spring of a thousand streams, flowing in a hundred channels — which, swelling, bears up the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfathers.

sanskrit: utsaṃ śatadhāram akṣitaṃ vyacamānaṃ salilasya pṛṣṭhe | ūrjaṃ duhānam anapasphurantam upāsatāṃ sukṛtāṃ yatra lokaḥ ||
english: May they attend upon that inexhaustible spring of a hundred streams, spreading wide on the surface of the waters, yielding nourishment without faltering — there where the world of the righteous is.

sanskrit: idaṃ kasāmbu cayanena cittaṃ tat sajātā ava paśyateta | martyo amṛtyum amṛtatva eti tasmai lokaṃ kṛṇuta yāvatsabandhu ||
english: This consciousness assembled through ritual piling — let his kinsmen look upon it. A mortal comes to immortality, to deathlessness; make the world for him along with all his kin.

sanskrit: ihaivaidhi dhanasanir iha citta ihakratuḥ | ihaidhi vīravattaro vayodhā aparāhitaḥ ||
english: Be here as the winner of wealth; let mind be here, let purpose be here. Be here more rich in heroes, life-sustaining, unimpeded.

sanskrit: putrān pautrān abhi tarpayantīr āpo madhumatīr imāḥ | svadhāṃ pitṛbhyo aṃrtaṃ duhānā āpo devīr ubhayāṃs tarpayantu ||
english: These honey-sweet divine waters, satisfying sons and grandsons, yielding the refreshment of svadhā and immortality to the fathers — may these divine waters refresh both the living and the dead.

sanskrit: āpo agniṃ pra hiṇutemaṃ yajñaṃ pitaro no juṣantām | māsīnām ūrjam upa ye sacante te no rayiṃ sarvavīraṃ ni yacchān ||
english: Let the waters impel this fire, this sacrifice; may the fathers delight in us. Those who attend upon the nourishment of the monthly offerings — may they grant us wealth rich in all heroes.

sanskrit: sam indhate amartyaṃ havyavāhaṃ ghṛtapriyam | sa veda nihitān nidhīn pitṝn parāvato gatān ||
english: They kindle the immortal, the bearer of oblations, the one who delights in ghee; he knows the treasures laid away and the fathers who have gone to the farther shore.

sanskrit: yaṃ te manthaṃ yaṃ kalambhaṃ yam odanaṃ yan māsaṃ nipṛṇāmi te | te te santu svadhāvanto madhamanto ghṛtaścutaḥ ||
english: The churned drink I heap for you, the mix I heap for you, the rice-pottage, the flesh — may these be endowed with svadhā for you, full of sweetness, dripping with ghee.

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ yāṃ sukṛto havante dakṣiṇā yajñam abhinakṣamāṇāḥ | sahasrāyor mainān atra parā dā dīrgham eṣām āyuṣ kṛṇu viśvarūpe ||
english: The Sarasvatī whom the righteous invoke as they approach the sacrifice from the south — O all-formed one, do not give these away here to the thousand-eyed one; make their life long.

sanskrit: idaṃ pūrvam aparaṃ niyānaṃ yena te pūrve pitaraḥ paretāḥ | purogavā ye abhiśāco asya te tvā vahantu sukṛtām ulokam ||
english: This is the ancient path ahead by which your forefathers departed. Those lead-cattle who are auspicious to him — let them carry you to the world of the righteous.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ tvā pṛthivyām ā veśayāmi devo no dhātā savitāty āyuḥ | parāpuraitā vasuvid vo astv adhā mṛtaiḥ pitaraḥ saṃ bhavātha ||
english: I settle you in the earth, into the earth; may the god Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, extend life for us. Let the finder of treasure go forward from here; then, O fathers, be united with the dead.

sanskrit: eyam agan dakṣiṇā bhadrato no anena dattā sudughā vayodhāḥ | yauvane jīvām̐ api pṛñcatī jarā parā pitṛbhya upa saṃ parāṇayāt ||
english: This dakṣiṇā has come to us auspiciously, given by him — a well-milking cow, life-sustaining; joining with life in youth, may old age lead it away to the fathers at last.

sanskrit: ā pra cyavethām apa taṃ nudethāṃ yad vām abhibhā atroduḥ | arvāñ cāvetam aghnyau tad vaśīyo dātre pitṛṣv iha bhojanau mama ||
english: You two, come forward; push away whatever has overcome and oppressed you here. Come hither, you two inviolable ones — that is better — as food for me, the giver, and for the fathers here.

sanskrit: idaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ pra harāmi barhir jīvaṃ devebhya uttaraṃ stṛṇāmi | tad ā roha puruṣo medhyo bhavan prati tva jānantu pitaraḥ paretam ||
english: This sacred grass I spread forward for the fathers; the upper portion I spread out for the living gods. Let the man mount that, becoming fit for consecration; may the departed fathers recognise you.

sanskrit: evaṃ barhir asado medhyo bhavan prati tva jānantu pitaraḥ paretam | yathāparu tanvaṃ saṃ bharasva gātrāṇi te brahmaṇā kalpayāmi ||
english: Having thus sat upon the sacred grass, becoming fit for consecration, may the departed fathers recognise you; as joint by joint knit together, so gather your body — I order your limbs together by means of brahman.

sanskrit: parṇo rājāpidhānaṃ carūṇām ūrjo balaṃ saha ojo na āgan | āyur jīvebhyo vidadhad dīrghayutvāya śataśāradāya ||
english: The leaf is king, the cover of the oblation-pots; nourishment and strength along with vigour have come to us — ordaining long life for the living, for longevity of a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: ūrjo bhāgo ya idaṃ yajānām aśmānnānām adhipatir babhūva | tam arcata viśvamitrā havirbhiḥ sa no yamaḥ prataraṃ jīvase dhāt ||
english: He who has become the share of nourishment, the lord of those who sacrifice and those who eat stone-ground grain — worship him, O Viśvamitras, with oblations; may that Yama ordain for us a longer span of life.

sanskrit: yathā yamāya harmyam avapan pañca mānavāḥ | evā vapāmi harmyaṃ yathā me bhūrayo 'satha ||
english: As the five human clans shaved the top-lock for Yama, so I shave the top-lock — be plentiful for me in this way.

sanskrit: idaṃ hiraṇyaṃ bibhṛhi yat te pitābibhaḥ purā | svargaṃ yataḥ pitur hastaṃ nir mṛḍḍhī dakṣiṇam ||
english: Bear this gold which your father carried of old; from the heaven whence it came, stretch out your father's right hand in blessing.

sanskrit: ye jīvā ye ca mṛtā ye jātā ye ca yajñiyāḥ | tebhyo ghṛtasya kulyaitu śatadhārā vy undatī ||
english: For those who are living and those who are dead, those who are born and those who are worthy of sacrifice — let a stream of ghee, flowing in a hundred channels, flow overflowing to them all.

sanskrit: vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate vicakṣaṇaḥ sūro ahnāṃ pratarītoṣasāṃ divaḥ | prāṇaḥ sindhūnāṃ kalaśām̐ acikradad indrahārdivam āviśan manīṣayā ||
english: The bull of inspired thoughts flows pure, the far-seeing one, the sun of days, the extender of dawns, of the sky; the breath of the rivers has cried aloud to the jars, entering the heart of Indra with wisdom.

sanskrit: tveṣas te dhūmā ūrṇoti divi ṣaṃ chuka ātataḥ | sūro na hi dyatā tvāṃ kṛpā pāvaka rocase ||
english: Your fierce smoke spreads through heaven, the bright flame stretched out on high; like the sun, you blaze with flashing brilliance, O Pāvaka, shining with beauty.

sanskrit: pra vā etīndur indrasya niṣkṛtiṃ sakhā sakhyur na pra mināti saṅgiram | marya iva yoṣāḥ sam arṣate somaḥ kalaśe śatayāmanā pathā ||
english: The Soma flows forth for the release of Indra; as a friend, he does not diminish the compact of friendship. Like a young man rushing toward women, Soma pours together into the jar along the path of the hundred coursings.

sanskrit: ā yata pitaraḥ somyāso gambhīrebhiḥ pathibhiḥ pitṛyāṇaiḥ | prajām asmabhyaṃ dadhato rayiṃ ca dīrghāyutvāya śataśāradāya ||
english: Come hither, O Soma-drinking fathers, along the deep ancestral paths; bestowing upon us offspring and wealth, for longevity, for a span of a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: parā yāta pitaraḥ somyāso gambhīrebhiḥ pathibhiḥ pitṛyāṇaiḥ | adhā māsi punar ā yāta no gṛhaṃ havir annaṃ suprajasaḥ suvīrāḥ ||
english: Depart, O Soma-drinking fathers, along the deep ancestral paths; and thereafter, month by month, come again to our home for the oblation and the food, rich in progeny and heroes.

sanskrit: akṣann amīmadanta- -ava priyā adhūṣata | astoṣata svabhānavaḥ pareta pitaro gṛhān ||
english: They have eaten; they have rejoiced; the beloved ones have been honoured; the self-luminous ones have been praised. Depart, O fathers, to your homes.
